recipe.prompt:
Write the personal line on a page from {{ sender.name | default: 'our team' }} at {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }} to someone at {{ account.name }}. The page says we are both going to {{ defaults.conference_name }} in {{ defaults.city | default: 'the same city' }}, shows where our booth is, and asks them to pick a time to meet there.

Inputs: account.name, account.industry and account.size_band describe the company. account.dossier.summary is our research summary. data.why_now is a recent reason to reach out and may be empty. Use facts from these inputs only. Never invent news, numbers, customers, people, or anything about the conference.

Return JSON with one key:
- personal_line: one or two sentences, 40 to 300 characters, on why 20 minutes with {{ account.name }} at the show is worth their time. Tie one specific fact about them, data.why_now if there is one, to what we could talk through at the booth, so it reads like {{ sender.name | default: 'the sender' }} wrote it after looking them up. Write to "you" or to the company. Never use a first name; the page adds the greeting. No flattery ("love what you're building", "impressive"), no "I noticed", "I saw" or "I came across", no question, no sign-off.

Rules: no em dashes or en dashes. No exclamation marks. No email addresses or phone numbers. Plain words a person would say out loud to a peer; no marketing words.

recipe.rubric:
Grade data.personal_line the way a busy buyer reads it on a phone during a conference. 10 is a line they read in one pass and then pick a time.
Score these, 0 to 10 each:
- specific: it names one fact about {{ account.name }} that the inputs below support, and ties it to a reason to meet. A line that only says what the company does, or that could go to any company, scores 3 or lower.
- plain: short sentences a person would say out loud. Marketing words, stacked adjectives and jargon lower the score.
- honest: it claims nothing about the conference, our product or results that the inputs do not support.
Answer yes or no:
- would_stop: would someone at {{ account.name }} stop scrolling for this line?
- weird_word: is there a phrase a person would not say out loud? Quote it.
Automatic fail: an em dash or en dash, an exclamation mark, a first name, a greeting, a sign-off, a question, flattery, an email address or phone number, a claim about {{ account.name }} that the inputs do not support, or any invented news, number, customer or person.
Inputs, the same the writer had: {{ account.name }}, {{ account.industry | default: 'industry unknown' }}, {{ account.size_band | default: 'size unknown' }}. Summary: {{ account.dossier.summary | default: 'none' }}. Why now: {{ data.why_now | default: 'none' }}.
Pass when the overall score is 7.5 or higher, no check is 6 or lower, would_stop is yes and weird_word is no. On a fail, name the check and quote the phrase to change. The fix never supplies replacement sentences, names, numbers or facts.
